subject: MSA / Order Form — provisional access, governing law & jurisdiction playbook
messages:
From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@orbitpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitpay.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: OrbitPay redlines: governing law + injunctive relief carveout

Neha — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has reviewed the MSA and attached our markups (OrbitPay_MSA_redlines.pdf). A couple of key items from legal that we need to flag up-front before we proceed to signature: 

- Governing law: OrbitPay is asking for New Jersey law instead of CA (state-level concern tied to our internal counsel).
- Jurisdiction / dispute resolution: they prefer a domestic federal court option rather than mandatory arbitration for injunctive relief. They will accept arbitration for money damages but want an express carveout allowing either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in state or federal court.
- Interim / provisional access: procurement requests clearer language enabling temporary access (read-only audit data exports) pending dispute escalation; they want explicit preservation obligations.

Attached is the redline. Can your legal team suggest a short rider or compromise language we can accept that preserves our ability to push arbitration but doesn't kill the deal? Also cc'ing procurement for transparency.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Ruiz
Head of Procurement | OrbitPay
Dana.ruiz@orbitpay.com
(555) 212-0987

Attachment: OrbitPay_MSA_redlines.pdf (PDF, 136 KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@orbitpay.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: OrbitPay redlines: governing law + injunctive relief carveout

Karthik / Marissa — looping you in. High-level ask from OrbitPay: move governing law to NJ and add a carveout to arbitration for provisional injunctive relief + an explicit temporary-access/preservation clause. Deal is mid-market, ARR ~ $420k, expected close this quarter (OP-2026-0192). Retail deal; procurement pushing hard on counsel.

Proposed approach (short):
1) Push to keep governing law as "California" but offer a tiered compromise: Governing law = California; enforcement of provisional injunctive relief may be sought in a court of competent jurisdiction (federal or state) where Venue = New Jersey if OrbitPay insists. This preserves our arbitration preference but provides convenience for OrbitPay counsel.

2) Arbitration carveout: Add narrow interim relief clause: "Notwithstanding the parties' agreement to arbitrate disputes, either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction to prevent irreparable harm; such action shall not constitute a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate the underlying dispute." Keep wording tight and limited to provisional injunctive relief.

3) Temporary access / preservation rider: Attach short rider (Redwood_provisional-relief-rider_v1.docx) that: (a) permits temporary read-only data export under an agreed MSA notice and audit process, (b) requires preservation of materials and CVs for 90 days pending escalation, and (c) includes a confidentiality carve for access logs.

I drafted the rider and the proposed one-paragraph arbitration carve. See attachments. If legal signs off, I think commercial can take these concessions given the size and speed to close.

Questions: is the NJ seat non-starter from a compliance or precedent POV? Karthik, any regulatory exposures?

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor | Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_provisional-relief-rider_v1.docx (DOCX, 18 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@orbitpay.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 13:17:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: OrbitPay redlines: governing law + injunctive relief carveout

Neha / Marissa / Dana — thanks for the clear summary and the draft rider. Quick read: I think the compromise Neha proposed is reasonable and narrow enough to keep our arbitration posture intact. A few redline suggestions (keeps changes minimal):

- Governing law: We should avoid a hard swap to NJ for all MSA governance. Offer a dual approach: "This Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of California without regard to conflict of law principles. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the parties agree that, for purposes of seeking provisional injunctive relief as described below, venue may be laid in the state or federal courts located in New Jersey if mutually agreed in writing prior to filing." That gives OrbitPay an option but requires a written pre-filing agreement to avoid unilateral forum shopping.

- Interim relief carveout (proposed language): "Notwithstanding the parties' agreement to resolve disputes through binding arbitration, either party may seek provisional injunctive relief or other urgent equitable remedies in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect confidentiality. The exercise of such rights shall not be deemed a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate the merits of any dispute." Keep "provisional" scope only.

- Preservation/temporary access rider: Trim the data export language to explicit read-only, with audit trail and RBAC restrictions. Add a 30-day preservation window (rather than 90) for logs and ephemeral caches — 30 days is more defensible operationally. Also include a requirement that OrbitPay raise the preservation/access request with 10 business days' notice except in emergency situations (self-certified emergency allowed).

I am fine with commercial approving these if OrbitPay accepts the written pre-filing agreement language. Marissa — if we accept NJ venue for provisional relief only with the pre-filing written consent requirement, are you ok from a T&Cs and precedent perspective?

Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 612-555-0174

From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@orbitpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitpay.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: OrbitPay redlines: governing law + injunctive relief carveout

Neha / Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the narrowly scoped language. We ran your suggested text by OrbitPay counsel this morning. Two points: 

1) Counsel wants to avoid a "pre-filing written agreement" requirement because in emergency situations we won't have time to coordinate that step. They asked to replace it with "or, in the case of emergency, any court of competent jurisdiction where interim relief is necessary." Karthik's carveout still limits scope to provisional injunctive relief which they find acceptable.

2) 30-day preservation window should be fine; OrbitPay will accept 30 days with a caveat: if additional preservation is required after initial 30 days, the parties will meet and confer in good faith to extend preservation.

If you can accept the emergency language tweak (we added a short parenthetical for emergencies) and the meet-and-confer extension path, we can sign and route via DocuSign. 

I attached a cleaned PDF with our comments (OrbitPay_MSA_redlines.pdf). Ready to proceed if Redwood agrees.

Best,
Dana
Dana Ruiz | Head of Procurement | OrbitPay
Dana.ruiz@orbitpay.com

Attachment: OrbitPay_MSA_redlines.pdf (clean copy, 118 KB)
